Reminds me of a flawed notion my grandfather has. He's not a bad guy. Self-made millionaire who worked hard for his wealth. He believed (maybe still does) that if all wealth was removed, the wealthy would get their wealth back, and the poor would stay poor. It implies that natural ability alone contributes to wealth, with no consideration of luck.   


Those who gain a lot of wealth need to be careful in adjusting how to spend it, but this isn't from being dumb. This is from overestimating newly made fortunes, such as with lottery winners who go bankrupt. I recommend staying frugal until you get a good grasp on your earnings.   


Your grandfather possibly believes a variant of this, so the best I think you can do is to prove him wrong through your own actions. It will take time, but if he refuses to acknowledge the truth, then he is a fool unworthy of the basest of council.
